title: The Layer That Can Take the Power Away: Torque Limits, Heat Derating, a Link Watchdog, an Emergency Stop, and Why Off Is Not Always Safe

questions.question: Why is off not always safe for a quadruped?
options: The motors heat up when the power is cut suddenly
The state machine loses track of where the legs are
A robot switched off while standing collapses and lands hard
The battery can be damaged by the sudden loss of load
questions.explanation: With no torque the legs fold and the body drops: the force of 35-09 on stiff legs. So off while standing is turned into soft, and the body is let down first.

questions.question: A torque command of 40 N m was cut to:
options: 40 N m, since the controller is trusted
0 N m: a command over the limit is refused whole
20 N m
10 N m, half the peak, to leave a margin
questions.explanation: Every joint's command is clipped to the motor's peak, in either direction. A controller that is wrong can ask for anything and cannot get more than that.

questions.question: Knees at 0.9 of their limit were derated to:
options: 0.90 of the torque, the same fraction as the heat
0.50 of the torque
0.25 of the torque
Nothing: at 0.9 the layer asks for off
questions.explanation: The torque is full up to 0.8 and falls in a straight line to nothing at 1.0, so 0.9 is half way. A quarter is what 0.95 gave.

questions.question: The emergency stop with the robot standing gave mode:
options: 2, soft
3, off
1, derated
0, normal, until the operator confirms
questions.explanation: The stop asks for off, and off while standing is turned into soft so that the body goes down gently. With the robot sitting the same stop gave 3.

questions.question: What does the layer take when several things are asked?
options: The first one asked, until it clears
The lowest mode that still deals with the most urgent
The highest mode, with the scale set back to 1
The highest mode, keeping the derating scale
questions.explanation: The modes are numbered by how much they take away, and the layer takes the highest asked. With hot knees and a silent link it chose soft and kept the derating as well.

questions.question: Is this a certified safety function?
options: Yes, because it outranks the controller
Yes, once its tests pass on every toolchain
Nearly: it only lacks a second sensor for the heat
No: a model of the logic; a real one runs on separate hardware with a hardware stop
questions.explanation: It is the logic, in the same program as the controller it limits. A safety function in the sense of 19-02 is separate hardware with its own stop.
